browserWalk.what: A 30-target Playwright walk of the deployed service, nine lenses plus six work views on each of template-city and empty-city, recording the visible lens set, rendered .basis and .state counts, rendered .pill text, DOM id count, hidden count, and two honest-absence guards.

Blocked-/app.js run: 30/30 ok, correct lens 2/30, 28 mismatches, and the distinct visible set across ALL 28 is exactly ["lens-city-manager"]. The two that pass are the two ?lens=city-manager requests, one per pack.
browserWalk.reading: That is the G-89 flash reproduced at browser level on the serving revision, comprehensively rather than on one sampled deep link: EVERY deep link that is not Overview paints Overview first. It is also the instrument watched failing before the fix, planner-side and independent of the executor's own.

gradingBaseline.what: Source-level census of web/index.html at main 6a4580d, for grading design PRs against.
gradingBaseline.values: 94 distinct ids with zero duplicates, 14 hidden attributes, 18 class="basis", 16 class="state", 15 distinct data-* hook names
gradingBaseline.independentCorroboration: The browser walk reports idsInDom 94 on the live DOM, matching the static census exactly.
gradingBaseline.freeFinding: The static file carries 14 hidden attributes and the live DOM carries 9. Two numbers that should agree and do not (DEV_PROCESS 1.4). Reconciled rather than rounded off: app.js un-hides five elements at runtime, which is the conditional-reveal behaviour working. The consequence for the item 7 instrument is that the hidden invariant must be asserted over the STATIC markup, never over a rendered DOM, or it would be red by design.

executorCP1Reviews.verdict: ACCEPTED, and it is stronger than the brief asked for
whatTheyDidBetter: Specificity was computed rather than argued: they parsed all 230 rules in web/shell.css, took the 68 that declare display, and filtered to those whose rightmost compound could match a section carrying an id in the fifteen and classes drawn from lens/on/roster-lens. Exactly two survive. They also checked that no @media, @supports or @container block mentions lens.

The JS-disabled requirement is met BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by care: the hide rules key on attribute PRESENCE (html[data-surface] .lens), so with scripting off no attribute is stamped, no hide rule applies, and the static class="lens on" governs exactly as it does today. That is better than the brief, which only asked them not to regress it.

They kept Playwright OUT of the repo, running it from the scratchpad, citing the product's own hidden-rule.test.mjs ruling that a test which quietly skips when Chrome is absent is a control that never fires. This was a trap the planner identified after dispatch and deliberately did NOT interrupt them about, on the reasoning that the signal was already in the repo and three running agents should not be interrupted for a maybe. The reasoning held.

They considered and rejected the one-rule :target alternative with a stated cost (it needs /#lens-finance, which breaks every existing deep link and every nav href), and named the rejection rather than silently not doing it.
They had already run the pre-fix browser leg and watched it fail before editing any product file.
executorCP1Reviews.twoIndependentMeasurementsAgree: Their pre-fix leg reports ?lens=finance with /app.js aborted showing ["lens-city-manager"], and unblocked showing ["lens-finance"]. The planner's own 30-target walk reports the identical result across 28 targets. Two instruments, built separately, agreeing.

recountConfirmed.countingRule: stylesheetClasses() in test/_lib.mjs: distinct class-selector tokens matching /[.](-?[_a-zA-Z][\w-]*)/g across vendor/sc-kit.css + vendor/shell.css, CRLF-normalized, CSS comments stripped first. State modifiers, element-scoped children and both theme classes count. Pseudo-classes, attribute selectors and element selectors are not classes and are not counted.
recountConfirmed.measuredNotDerived: They took the before set from `git show HEAD:vendor/*.css` and the after set from the re-vendored tree, both measured, never derived by subtraction (DEV_PROCESS 1.3). 109 before, 139 after, 30 added, 0 removed.
recountConfirmed.gateWatchedRed: npm test went 74 pass / 0 fail to 72 pass / 2 fail. The two failures are the size pin (139 !== 109) and the coverage assertion naming exactly the thirty added classes, 109 of 139 covered, 78.4 percent. The uncovered list IS the work list and nothing else regressed.

executorCP1Reviews.reconciliationOwedByThePlannerAndNowPaid: The css-families investigation predicted 138 and the WDLL carried 138 as an estimate. The measured 139 reconciles exactly: 109 + 19 for the three named families + 11 for the finding family, where the eleventh is the meter fill token `f`. The investigation itself flagged `f` parenthetically ('the meter fill f makes 11 if .f is not already counted') and then dropped it from its own headline. `f` was not already counted. So the two numbers that should agree now do, and the discrepancy was a token lost between a parenthesis and a total.
namingFindingsAccepted: `rail` now carries three unrelated meanings in one token: the .srcreg severity rail, the .colstack.rail 380px layout modifier, and the new .mxrow > .rail and .finding > .rail. No CSS conflict and every rule is scoped. Recorded rather than renamed, correctly: renaming a shipped class is a product-line change across three byte-locked repos, not a kit PR.
`c` and `f` are one-character tokens and are the two least greppable in the vocabulary. Both element-scoped, neither emitted bare.

executorCP1Reviews.verdict: ACCEPTED, and it corrected the planner in four places
correctionsToThePlannerFigures: 94 ids and 14 hidden CONFIRMED, and they established page-wide equals index.html positively by measuring that shell-homes.mjs, staff-map.mjs and staff-review.mjs emit zero ids, rather than assuming it.
'10 querySelectorAll' is an UNDERSTATEMENT of reach: there are a further 10 querySelector and 3 closest call sites carrying selector strings, one of which addresses an id (#ds-metrics).

The planner's eight data-* names were wrong in both directions. data-disposition is read by shell.css, not by app.js, so it is not a script hook at all. And the list omitted data-metric, data-stage-max and data-theme.

They split the hook population into two sets with separate bases, script-read (10) and stylesheet-read (2), because the class rule counts classes and never looks at attribute selectors, and shell.css colours the connections register, the largest section of the page at 446 elements, entirely off data-disposition.
executorCP1Reviews.trap2SolvedByDerivation: Rather than a hand-written allow-list, the instrument scans served scripts for id-WRITING expressions (.id =, setAttribute("id"), id=" inside template literals) and subtracts what a script creates from what it must find. Measured empty today, and stated as a positive determination with its basis (13 createElement calls assigning className, textContent and dataset; .id on none; setAttribute only with aria-selected and aria-expanded) rather than as an empty result. That is the correct answer to the has_writer defect class: a declaration nothing recomputes is exactly what is being avoided.
executorCP1Reviews.presenceNotValueWithAMeasuredBasis: The hook rule asserts attribute PRESENCE, and the basis is measured rather than asserted: sc-kit.css line 29 selects :root:not([data-theme="light"]), so data-theme="light" is styled and deliberately never attached in static markup. A value-level rule would be red on day one, which DEV_PROCESS 2.0 forbids. Presence is also precisely the property a React translation loses.

rulingsTaken.subject: the root attribute is data-surface, not data-lens
rulingsTaken.why: A-072 wrote 'stamps data-lens on the root'. That was planner scoping language about the mechanism, not an operator ruling on the attribute NAME, and the executor found a concrete collision the planner had not: data-lens ALREADY exists in this document, on the fifteen nav anchors, carrying a DIFFERENT value vocabulary. The nav carries the bare lens id (finance); the root needs the section id (lens-finance). Two value vocabularies under one attribute name is the naming trap this program flags early, and html[data-lens] would additionally start matching any future querySelectorAll for [data-lens]. data-surface is the product's own word for these fifteen things.
rulingsTaken.consequenceNamed: A-072's text now diverges from what shipped. The row is amended rather than left to disagree with the code.

rulingsTaken.subject: the fix extends to the Development-services tabs and the Assets tabs
rulingsTaken.ruling: ACCEPTED as scope, widened beyond A-072's letter, with the reason recorded.
rulingsTaken.why: A-072 scoped the flash at the lens axis. The same mechanism governs the six DS tabs (.ds-tab) and the three Assets tabs (.assets-tab): a static .on in the document, a class app.js toggles after the deferred module runs. Fixing only the lens axis ships half a fix and leaves a deep link to ?lens=development-services&tab=review painting Pipeline first. 27 enumerated selectors in total (15 surfaces + 6 DS tabs + 3 Assets tabs + 3 presence-keyed hide rules), kept in step by a three-way set-equality test across staff-review.mjs, index.html and shell.css.

newFindingsThisCheckpoint.finding: Two data-* hooks are emitted into shipped markup and read by nothing at all.
newFindingsThisCheckpoint.measured: The planner's markup census finds 15 distinct data-* names. B887's derivation finds 12 that any script or stylesheet reads. The three-name difference is data-home-row, data-home-table and data-source. Of those, data-home-row IS read, by src/server.test.mjs and src/shell-homes.test.mjs, so a test is a legitimate reader and it is live. data-home-table (70 occurrences) and data-source (1 occurrence) are emitted by src/shell-homes.mjs and appear in web/index.html and are referenced by no script, no stylesheet and no test. 71 attribute occurrences with no reader.
newFindingsThisCheckpoint.class: Same shape as roster-lens: shipped, and defined or read nowhere.
newFindingsThisCheckpoint.disposition: NOT acted on. Carried to the design pass, where the Connections PR edits connectionsRegisterHtml() and the roster PR already carries the roster-lens deletion. Deleting emitted markup is a product change and does not belong in a test-only PR.
